integration_issues.flow: Weekly task persistence (Friday / weekdays / custom days)
integration_issues.issue: storage.saveTasks() maps tasks to only {id,title,slot,createdAt} and DROPS the `days` field. In localStorage, days becomes undefined => a Friday-only or custom-days task loses its schedule on reload and starts appearing every day. Reproduction: create Friday task -> reload -> localStorage.getItem('salah_first_tasks') shows no `days` -> task visible today (dow=3, Wed) even though it should only appear Fridays.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix storage.saveTasks() to preserve `days` field. Change the destructure to `.map(({ id, title, slot, days, createdAt }) => ({ id, title, slot, days: days ?? null, createdAt: createdAt || Date.now() }))` in /app/frontend/src/lib/storage.js. Without this fix, the entire weekly-task feature (repeat-friday, repeat-weekdays, repeat-custom) is silently broken across reloads.
OPTIONAL: expose data-testid="streak" / "xp" / "next-prayer" on StatsBar for future regression scripts (currently only the container is testable).

context_for_next_testing_agent: The weekly-task days-not-persisted bug is in storage.saveTasks (drops days on destructure). It is pre-existing (predates this polish iteration) but is user-visible only after a page reload; the current in-memory filter still hides Friday tasks correctly within the same session, which is why previous iterations reported it as PASS. Verify fix by: (1) create Friday task, (2) reload page, (3) confirm localStorage entry has days:[5] and task is hidden on non-Fridays.
rca of the issue: storage.js:saveTasks(tasks) does `tasks.map(({ id, title, slot, createdAt }) => ({ id, title, slot, createdAt: createdAt || Date.now() }))`. The `days` property is not destructured and therefore never written to localStorage. HomePage.handleAddTask correctly passes `days` when constructing the new task object and updates React state with it (which is why in-session filtering works), but the saveTasks call strips it before persistence. On reload, getTasksList returns tasks without days -> filter treats them as everyday tasks. Fix: include days in the destructure and in the returned object (with `days: days ?? null`).
